reviews.title: Manus: Unacceptable Support During a Major Data-Restoration Failure
reviews.text:
I originally found Manus genuinely useful and invested significant time building websites, applications, and other important projects on the platform.

Unfortunately, the recent data-restoration process became an absolute nightmare.

After my data was marked as successfully restored, significant portions of my work were still missing. It took approximately one month and countless hours of emails and support conversations to get the issue resolved. During that time, I repeatedly received conflicting information, was transferred between support conversations, and was often given generic responses that failed to address the actual technical problem.

The most frustrating part was dealing with what appeared to be automated AI support agents that repeatedly asked me to explain the same situation, requested irrelevant screenshots, or directed me toward basic troubleshooting—even though this was clearly a data-recovery issue.

While I am grateful that my data was eventually recovered, the amount of time, stress, and uncertainty involved was unacceptable. My website and related work were unavailable during this process, which affected my ability to operate my counseling practice and potentially cost me prospective clients.

I cannot confidently recommend Manus for business-critical work when the data-restoration process is this unreliable and meaningful technical support is so difficult to access.

The technology may have potential, but data reliability, customer support, and account

reviews.title: Expensive
reviews.text:
The AI itself is really good and does its job well. My main issue is the pricing and credit system.

I pay £20 per month for 4,000 points. I needed to make just one change to my website, and a single request used around 3,900 points. That left me with only 100 points, even though I had paid for my subscription just three days earlier.

Now I basically have to wait almost a whole month to receive another 4,000 points. For me, this makes the service extremely expensive compared with other AI tools on the market.

For comparison, I use OpenAI Codex on the same website and can make hundreds of changes without running into this kind of credit limitation.

The AI is very good, but the current credit system makes it difficult to justify the subscription. £20 for effectively one website change is simply too expensive.

reviews.title: An Expensive Masterclass in Unfulfilled Potential
reviews.text:
I have spent hundreds of dollars on Manus over the past year, which makes this review particularly disappointing because I used to be one of its strongest advocates. The concept is brilliant. The vision is compelling. Unfortunately, the execution has become an increasingly frustrating exercise in lowered expectations.

Manus has developed a remarkable habit of confidently announcing that a task is complete while leaving behind little evidence that anything has actually been completed. Missing deliverables, unfinished outputs, broken functionality, and abandoned processes have become far too common. The only thing that appears consistently reliable is the consumption of credits.

What makes this so maddening is that the platform clearly possesses enormous potential. Yet instead of accelerating productivity, it often requires users to double-check, troubleshoot, restart, and repeat work that should have been finished correctly the first time. Every new task now feels less like an opportunity and more like a gamble.

For a platform positioning itself as a serious partner in building products and businesses, reliability should not feel like a pleasant surprise. Manus remains an exceptional idea, but the widening gap between what it promises and what it routinely delivers has become impossible to ignore. I wanted to remain a champion of this platform. Lately, it feels as though I am merely funding its ongoing apprenticeship.

reviews.title: Active Pro User Unable to Purchase Credits for Days
reviews.text:
I wanted to like Manus and the platform itself has a lot of potential, but my experience with support and billing has been extremely frustrating.

I am a paid Manus Pro subscriber and used my included monthly credits. When I attempted to purchase additional credits, every purchase failed with Apple’s “Your purchase could not be completed” error.

Before contacting support, I spent hours troubleshooting:

• Updated the app
• Restarted devices
• Tested on both iPhone and iPad
• Signed out and back into Media & Purchases
• Tried multiple payment methods
• Added an entirely different debit card
• Verified Apple Cash worked
• Verified other App Store purchases worked successfully

The problem only occurred with Manus purchases.

Support repeatedly pointed me toward Apple, despite the fact that other App Store purchases worked without issue. After extensive back-and-forth, support eventually acknowledged there was a backend synchronization issue on my account. However, I still could not purchase credits and was left waiting for technical review without a clear timeline for resolution.

The most frustrating part was spending significant time troubleshooting and being sent in circles between Apple-related explanations and Manus support before the account issue was finally acknowledged.

The software itself has promise, but if you rely on it for work, be aware that billing and account issues can leave you unable to purchase credits when you need them most, and support resolution may n

reviews.title: Manus AI is the worst (scam)
reviews.text:
Manus AI is impressive in demos, but real-world use has been frustrating.

The biggest problem is how fast it burns through credits while trying to fix its own mistakes. You end up paying premium pricing just to babysit the AI while it breaks layouts, misunderstands instructions, or loops through tasks incorrectly.

The concept is great. The execution still feels early.

I also noticed that the more complex the project gets, the less reliable the output becomes. It works better building something from scratch than trying to edit or improve an existing project. Once you start making revisions, things can spiral fast.

The marketing makes it seem like you can replace entire teams overnight. In reality, you still need experience to catch problems before they turn into bigger ones.

There’s definitely potential there, but right now it feels more like an expensive beta test than a polished business tool.

Subject: Serious Feedback Regarding Recent Policy Changes and Free Access
To the Manus Team,
I am writing this to express my deep disappointment regarding the current direction of the platform. To be blunt: Manus is not what it used to be. Initially, Manus stood out as a revolutionary tool that prioritized user experience and accessibility. However, the recent restrictions on free chat and the aggressive shift towards a "pay-to-play" model have alienated a huge portion of your core community. You’ve moved away from the innovative spirit that made us trust you in the first place, becoming just another restricted service behind a paywall.
The free chat wasn't just a "feature"—it was the heart of the platform that allowed users to explore the AI’s potential without constant limitations. By restricting it so heavily, you are killing the creativity and the daily engagement that built your reputation.
We strongly urge you to reconsider these changes and bring back a functional free chat tier. Listen to your users before the loyalty you’ve built vanishes completely. We want the "Old Manus" back—the one that actually cared about its community’s accessibility.
Looking forward to seeing actual changes, not just automated responses.

reviews.title: Just not ready
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like Manus AI. On the surface it looks impressive. Clean UI, ambitious capabilities, and a strong promise of autonomous task completion. Unfortunately, in practice, it struggles to reliably finish what it starts.

It does generate outputs, but when asked to complete multi-step tasks it often gets stuck in loops. It appears to be working toward the goal, but repeatedly attempts similar approaches, fails, retries, and consumes credits the entire time.

I tested the Pro plan by asking it to generate some images and upload them to Google Drive. Instead of taking a straightforward approach, it decided to build out a Google Cloud API workflow using gcloud utilities to upload the files. Technically feasible, yes — but massively over-engineered for the task. It then became stuck creating folders in my Drive and ended up generating 93 folders with the same name. It repeatedly claimed files had been uploaded, but every folder was empty.

After about 1.5 hours of this, I had run out of credits.

I recognise that non-deterministic AI systems are inherently difficult to control and evaluate. However, charging premium pricing while the agent repeatedly fails, loops, and burns through credits creates a frustrating experience. It feels expensive for the level of reliability currently delivered.

There is clear promise here. The concept is strong, and when it works, it looks powerful. But right now, it feels like a beta product being priced as a mature one. Promising… just

reviews.title: Unauthorized Credit Deduction
reviews.text:
I requested Manus to pause all automated updates to my connected Notion accounts and received an explicit system acknowledgment stating it would “hold off on any further changes” until I gave the go-ahead. This was not done under my personal Apple account, but rather, a Manus-specific account tied to my business.

Despite that confirmation, Manus continued running automated tasks over multiple days, deducting 1,221 in credits after authorization had been withdrawn. When I contacted support, I was told this did not qualify for a refund.

Until Manus can honor explicit pause requests or take responsibility when it doesn’t, I can’t recommend trusting it with live integrations or paid credits.

reviews.title: No Response From Support
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, my experience with Manus AI has been extremely disappointing. The system has bugs that stop projects from moving forward, and when that happens, they push everything to the AI even issues that clearly require a human developer. The problem is that when they say a human will review it, no one ever replies.
I waited over 48 hours multiple times without any response, and my project remained completely stuck because of their system’s errors.
It’s frustrating to invest time, money, and trust into a platform that shows no real commitment to its users when a serious issue arises.
The technology is great, but the company fails at the basics: support, responsibility, and respect for the customer. I hope they improve, because as of now, I cannot recommend it.
